questions.q: Is LTV Global, the company used throughout this capstone, a real business?
options: No — it is explicitly a fictional, illustrative company invented for this capstone
Yes — it is a real multinational consumer-products company
Yes — it is a real company with its name changed for privacy
The lesson deliberately leaves this unclear
questions.explain: The lesson repeatedly and explicitly labels LTV Global as fictional and illustrative, never a real company, consistent with this catalog's policy on invented scenarios.

questions.q: Which fictional system is the ERP and system of record for orders and products at LTV Global?
options: Atlas
Beacon
Comet
Harbor
questions.explain: Atlas is the core ERP running on SQL Server, holding dbo.Customers, dbo.Orders, dbo.OrderLines, dbo.Products, and dbo.Payments.

questions.q: What specific incident triggered LTV Global's decision to build a real governance program?
options: A UK customer's data subject access request took six weeks to answer, and two systems returned conflicting order histories for the same person
A competitor announced a new product line
The company's warehouse system went offline for a day
An employee asked for a raise
questions.explain: The DSAR gap — six weeks, four departments, and two conflicting order histories for one person — is the concrete incident that reached the board and triggered the mandate.

questions.q: Who sponsors the data governance program this capstone follows?
options: Dana Whitfield, the newly hired Chief Data Officer
A customer in Leeds
The warehouse management vendor
No one — the program has no sponsor
questions.explain: The board gave newly hired CDO Dana Whitfield the mandate and budget to stand up the program, making her the executive sponsor for this capstone's scenario.

questions.q: Which three systems each hold a separate, currently unreconciled copy of "customer" data at LTV Global?
options: Atlas, Beacon, and Comet
Harbor, Summit, and Atlas
Beacon, Harbor, and Summit
Only Comet holds customer data
questions.explain: Atlas (ERP), Beacon (CRM), and Comet (e-commerce) each capture their own version of a customer record today, which is exactly the problem later lessons resolve.
